newsitem.title: FRANCE: Petrol bombs hit Corsica gendarmerie barracks.
newsitem.headline: Petrol bombs hit Corsica gendarmerie barracks.

text.p: Suspected Corsican separatists threw petrol bombs at two para-military gendarmerie barracks on the eve of a visit to the island by French Defence Minister Charles Millon, the gendarmerie said on Thursday.
The attacks, in Porto-Vecchio and Figari in the south of the French Mediterranean island on Wednesday, caused damage, with three cars partly or completely burnt out, but no injuries.

Separatist sympathisers had demonstrated outside the Porto-Vecchio barracks to protest at the detention of three people in an investigation into a bombing and alleged extortion attempt at the Sperone golf course in December.
Over the past eight months, gendarmerie offices have reported some 40 machinegun attacks.
Millon was due to arrive at the Solenzara military base on the island's east coast later on Thursday and meet gendarmerie chiefs of staff in the capital Ajaccio.
Police said on Wednesday they had detained a total of 10 people for questioning in connection with the golf course probe.
Three of those in custody were suspected of being intermediaries in the alleged scheme to extort protection money from the golf course owner by bombing it, police said.
Such payments are known in Corsica as a "revolutionary tax" demanded by separatists engaged in a two-decade-old campaign for increased autonomy from mainland France.
A top leader of the political wing of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), Francois Santoni, was already in custody in connection with the scheme, the police said.
